entries.speaker: EXPERT-PRIOR
entries.role: statistical expert; k-NN over 8 structured variables of THIS prompt only, trained on 91 labelled cases, leave-one-out honest
entries.title: INITIAL RECOMMENDATION (statistical prior)
entries.body:
A basic classifier, whose sole purpose is to provide a suggestion, produces this result along with its associated uncertainty. The purpose of this decision is to use it as an initial reference point for discussing the results.

SUGGESTION: BIOPSY
  p(biopsy = yes) = 0.56 +/- 0.20   (95% CI 0.17-0.90)

Where the uncertainty comes from:
  - aleatoric  dA = 0.15  (the nearest labelled cases disagree with each other)
  - epistemic  dA = 0.13  (few labelled cases resemble this one)
  - 7.5 effective neighbours out of 10; 3 of the 5 closest labelled cases were biopsied
  - 80%-coverage conformal set: {no, yes}

TIER 'discuss': A +/- dA straddles 0.5. The classifier genuinely CANNOT tell these two answers apart; measured accuracy in this tier is 0.61, barely above the 0.62 majority-class rate. Its number is a starting point only, and the case must be decided on the clinical evidence retrieved by the other participants.

Variables it actually read (from the visible panel only, no documents retrieved):
  pirads=4.0, bx_ord=3.0, psa=5.2, age=68.0, psad=0.151, dre_ord=0.0, vol=34.49, n_pmhx=0.0
  missing / not evaluable: none

Out-of-fold performance of this recommender on the 91 labelled cases (5x5 CV):
  accuracy 0.703, balanced accuracy 0.662, AUC 0.75, ECE 0.095.
It is right about 7 times out of 10 overall. It is NOT an oracle and it has never seen the
radiology report, the PSA trajectory, the laboratory panel or the previous notes.

data.lectura: A ± ΔA cruza 0.5: el recomendador NO distingue. Escribir el número en la pizarra como punto de partida y dejar que los demás expertos lo muevan; aquí acierta poco más que la clase mayoritaria.
data.nota_entrenamiento: El caso está entre los 91 etiquetados; se ha excluido de sus propios vecinos, así que esta respuesta es honesta.

entries.speaker: LLM-1-GAP-ANALYST
entries.role: raises doubt only; has no access to clinical documents and issues no recommendation
entries.title: GAPS AND DOUBTS
entries.body:
WHAT THE PRIOR CANNOT SEE
  The statistical recommender relied only on the structured panel. It could not weigh the patient's PSA velocity (1.62 ng/mL/yr) against the PI-RADS 4 score, which is a key dynamic factor. It also could not incorporate the PSA history trend (prior PSA 4.2 ng/mL) to assess the rate of rise, which is crucial for risk stratification. Finally, it could not integrate the specific findings from the mpMRI report or the full laboratory panel, which are necessary to contextualize the PI-RADS 4 score and PSA density.

WHY THE SUGGESTION COULD BE WRONG
  The prior suggests BIOPSY with a wide interval (0.56 +/- 0.20), indicating it is in the 'discuss' tier. A failure mode is the potential contradiction between the PI-RADS 4 score and the Normal DRE, which might suggest a lower likelihood of clinically significant cancer than the PSA velocity might imply. Another failure mode is the prior positive biopsy status, which makes the question "does he have cancer" less relevant than assessing the current risk profile based on the new imaging and trend data.

WHAT TO RETRIEVE, AND WHAT WOULD CHANGE THE ANSWER
  <document> radiology / mpMRI report -> If the report details significant intraprostatic extension or high-risk features, it would increase the need for biopsy.
  <document> PSA history (trend) -> If the trend shows a rapid, concerning rise, it would increase the need for biopsy.
  <document> laboratory results (full panel) -> If the lab panel shows any markers (e.g., inflammation, other cancers) that modify the risk, it would change the decision.
  <document> previous GP / urology consultation notes -> If these notes detail the clinical reasoning for the prior positive biopsy, it would contextualize the current re-evaluation.

WHAT THE EVIDENCE SUPPORTS

entries.title: FINAL DECISION AND FORM
entries.body:
FINAL DECISION: BIOPSY   (confidence: clear)

Biopsy is recommended because the evidence strongly supports sampling due to the high-risk PI-RADS 4 lesion in the right anterior mid-gland and the rising PSA velocity of 1.62 ng/mL/yr. This is further supported by the prior positive biopsy result and the significant PSA rise from 4.2 ng/mL to 5.2 ng/mL over approximately one year. The statistical prior suggested biopsy, and the retrieved evidence converges on this recommendation.
